claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To give you an accurate assessment, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm inquiring about one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

Now, let me ask you some questions to determine if you meet the eligibility criteria:

**Is Alex under the age of 16, or is he aged 16-19 and in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 18 and still in education - he's doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful to know.

**Does Alex live with you?** (i.e., is he your dependent child living in your household?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and maintenance?** (In other words, do you provide for his everyday needs and upkeep?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am - I provide for all his everyday needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Before I make my final determination, let me check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I have all the details correct.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need to make my determination. Based on the eligibility rules and the information you've provided, I can provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

✓ **Age and education:** Alex is 18 and in approved full-time education (A-levels). You can claim Child Benefit for children aged 16 or over if they're in approved education or training, up until age 20.

✓ **Living arrangements:** Alex lives with you in your household.

✓ **Responsibility for care and maintenance:** You provide for all his everyday needs.

All the key requirements are met, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for him. If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can apply through HMRC.

reasonings: Alex meets all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit: (1) He is 18 years old and still in approved education (A-levels), which means he qualifies under the rule that allows Child Benefit to continue for children aged 16 or over who stay in approved education or training until age 20. (2) He lives with you, his parent. (3) You are responsible for his care and maintenance, providing for all his everyday needs. All three key requirements are satisfied.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. He qualifies because he is under 20 and remains in approved full-time education (A-levels), lives with you, and you provide for his everyday needs and maintenance.">
